idiom_name: case object NoOp / Option (None) with getOrElse and foreach
implementation_notes: Scala's standard answer to absence is Option: None is itself a case object implementing the whole Option protocol neutrally (isEmpty, getOrElse, map, toList), so an optional collaborator is normally a value the caller folds rather than a nullable reference. When the collaborator must be non-null the null object costs one declaration - case object NullLogger extends Logger { def log(msg: String): Unit = () } - a singleton with pattern-matchable identity, and Nil plays the same role for lists. Use Option/Either when absence must be handled; use the case object when callers should call unconditionally.
pitfalls: Option and a null object solve different problems: Some(NullLogger) is still Some, so wrapping a null object in Option creates two encodings of 'absent' that different call sites read differently.
null is still reachable through Java interop (Map.get, platform types); wrap Java results with Option(...) at the boundary and keep the null object for your own interfaces.
A case object is initialised once per JVM; keep it stateless, and never compare with == to detect the null case when the interface is open to other implementations.
